recentItems.title: Suspected pneumonic Siberian plague outbreak ‘suggests engineering’ says journalist
recentItems.description:
Hundreds of people in eastern Russia have been placed in quarantine after a laboratory worker died of suspected pneumonic plague.

Darya Shipolova was an employee of the Anti-Plague Research Institute in Siberia and people thought to have had contact with her are reportedly being isolated.

Annie Jacobsen, author of ‘Biological War: A Scenario’, which examines the potential consequences of a large-scale biological attack or the accidental release of a pathogen tells Channel 4 News the circumstances "suggests engineering" which is "troubling".

recentItems.title: Comedian jailed for joke in Turkey
recentItems.description:
A Turkish comedian was sentenced to more than 19 months imprisonment for insulting the President and religious values.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Deniz Göktaş has been released pending appeal, but still spent 88 days in jail after clips of his show, including a reference to President Erdogan as a “dictator”,  went viral.

The comedian told a courtroom last week that he stood by his joke describing Erdogan as having evolved from a “shy dictator” to one “confident in his identity".

recentItems.title: Watch as Saudi-backed forces repel Houthi advances in Yemen
recentItems.description:
In Yemen, Saudi-backed government forces say they have attacked hundreds of Houthi targets, retaking key areas around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait along the Red Sea coast.

The Yemeni government says it has secured effective control of the vital oil route. 

This surge in fighting is bringing yet more potential consequences for the soaring price of oil, pushing global prices even higher.

recentItems.title: US sends mixed messages over RAF Fairford bomber withdrawal
recentItems.description:
There have been mixed messages from the United States about the withdrawal of its bombers from RAF Fairford after a suspected terror plot targeting the base.

Downing Street insists the Gloucestershire air base is safe and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he wouldn't directly tie last week's arrests to the decision to move the bombers. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

But Vice President JD Vance said it was due to an abundance of caution over what Iran might be doing, and US officials told The New York Times that the redeployment had been ordered after more details about threats to the base emerged at the weekend.

This is in line with Iran's position that military bases used to bomb Iran are legitimate targets. 

So, how safe are the bases and does it change what America can do if it re-starts the bombing of Iran?

recentItems.title: Why has America suddenly PULLED its bombers out of Britain?
recentItems.description:
The sudden withdrawal of American heavy bombers from RAF Fairford back to the United States follows a major incident near the Gloucestershire airbase. Five men were arrested near the base, with the UK government saying it showed "strong indications" of state-sponsored involvement from Tehran.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

So why has the US pulled its bombers from the UK? Has the abrupt departure handed Tehran a tactical and propaganda victory? And what does the saga say about the UK’s special relationship with the US?

On this episode of the Fourcast, Krishnan Guru-Murthy is joined by Dr David Jordan from the Freeman Air and Space Institute, former senior official at the Pentagon, Jim Townsend, as well as Trita Parsi from the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft.
